scope: Proposition 2.5 (Reduction to a box solution) of the manuscript “Randomized quasipolynomial-time mean-payoff games” (preprints/Randomized-quasipolynomial-time-mean-payoff-games-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 104 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4ab7552f58266134), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let x solve the constant box [0, B∗], with B∗ = 8nW as in Equation (2.1). Then the original game’s exact zero-threshold winning set is U = {i ∈ V : xi > B∗/2}. A positional Max strategy guarantees original mean payoff at least zero from every vertex of U. Outside U, a positional Min strategy ensures that every consistent play has original upper limiting average at most −1/n, including against arbitrary history-dependent Max strategies.
